name: Sudanese Nationals Travelling on a Foreign Passport

requirements.blocker_text: Holds a Sudanese identity document, evidencing Sudanese nationality, despite travelling on a foreign passport.
A Sudanese sponsor's identity document must be submitted with the application.

outcome.duration_length: USD 154 fee; up to 10 working days processing; specific stay duration not stated by the source

sources.title: Embassy of the Republic of Sudan -- Entry Visa, 'Sudanese Nationals with Foreign Passports' category: USD 154, up to 10 working days, requires a Sudanese ID document and a Sudanese sponsor's ID

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Sudan). STATUS: PUBLISHED -- tier-1 official diplomatic mission sourced. This is a facilitation category for people who ARE Sudanese nationals under Sudan's own Nationality Act but hold and travel on a foreign passport -- distinct from a true diaspora/ancestry-exemption route like Bangladesh's NVR or Fiji's Exemption by Descent, since it presupposes the applicant already IS a current Sudanese national (evidenced by a Sudanese ID), not merely of Sudanese origin or descent. Its practical relevance is shaped by Sudan's Nationality Act not generally recognizing dual citizenship (see sd_citizenship_naturalisation.json's notes on the Act's silence on dual citizenship generally, and its explicit automatic-revocation rule specifically for South Sudanese citizenship) -- meaning a person using this category is, on paper, solely a Sudanese national who happens to hold a second country's travel document, a status whose legal footing may be more precarious than the visa process itself suggests. work_rights/study_rights modeled as 'full' on the reasoning that a person entering on their own nationality's documentation is not visa-restricted the way a foreign national would be, though this is an inference from the category's structure rather than an explicit tier-1 statement to that effect.
